entries.summary: The CVMP granted a positive opinion for a marketing authorisation of Bovilis Lumpyvax in exceptional circumstances.
entries.why_it_matters: This approval enables the product to be marketed in the EU; RA teams should update regulatory dossiers and launch plans accordingly.

entries.label: EMA Guidelines
entries.title: Questions and answers on the PIP compliance verification procedure at EMA, and on paediatric rewards
entries.description: Questions and answers on the PIP compliance verification procedure at EMA, and on paediatric rewards
entries.summary: EMA provides clarification on the PIP compliance verification procedure and paediatric rewards.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must be aware of updated procedures for PIP compliance and paediatric reward calculations.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Notice of Compliance (NOC) Data Extracts
entries.description: The data extract is a series of compressed ASCII text files of the Notice of Compliance (NOC) database.
entries.summary: Release of Notice of Compliance (NOC) database extracts in compressed ASCII text files.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams can use the extracted NOC data for compliance tracking and monitoring of approved products.

entries.label: EMA News
entries.title: Clinical trial applications advice pilot becomes permanent
entries.description: The Accelerating Clinical Trials in the EU (ACT EU) advice pilot, which helps sponsors prepare clinical trial applications, will become a permanent initiative from January 2027…
entries.summary: The ACT EU advice pilot, which assists sponsors in preparing clinical trial applications, will now become a permanent initiative effective January 2027.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams across all therapeutic areas must be aware that permanent guidance support will be available, impacting their application preparation timelines and resource planning.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Product monograph brand safety updates
entries.description: Product monograph brand safety updates for Submissions cleared between 01-09-2026 and 30-09-2026
entries.summary: Brand safety guidelines in product monographs have been updated.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must review the updated safety sections for all submissions cleared in September 2026 to ensure compliance.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Guide to reporting and providing information on drug shortages and discontinuations (GUI-0120)
entries.description: This document is intended to help market authorization holders comply with sections C.01.014.8 to C.01.014.91 of the Food and Drug Regulations
entries.summary: The FDA provides a guide to reporting and providing information on drug shortages and discontinuations to aid compliance with specific sections of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams must use this guide to ensure they meet reporting obligations under sections C.01.014.8 to C.01.014.91.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Guide to distributing drugs intended for the Canadian market for consumption or use outside Canada (GUI-0145)
entries.description: This document is intended to help drug establishment licence holders comply with sections C.01.014.94 to C.01.014.95 of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.summary: The guide clarifies how drug establishment licence holders must distribute Canadian-market drugs for use outside Canada, aligning with sections C.01.014.94 to C.01.014.95 of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams that license and supply drugs internationally must update their distribution processes to ensure compliance with the specified regulatory sections.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Guide on the exceptional importation and sale of drugs in response to shortages and discontinuations (GUI-0148)
entries.description: This document will help drug establishment licence holders comply with sections C.10.004 to C.10.013 of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.summary: The guide introduces new procedures for the exceptional importation and sale of drugs to address shortages and discontinuations.
entries.why_it_matters: Drug establishment licence holders must follow the updated sections C.10.004 to C.10.013 of the Food and Drug Regulations to legally import and sell drugs under exceptional circumstances.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Guide on extending expiration dates of marketed drugs in response to drug shortages (GUI-0500)
entries.description: This document will help market authorization holders and drug establishment licence holders understand how to comply with sections C.010.014 to C.10.021 of the Food and Drug Regulations
entries.summary: This guide explains how to legally extend the expiration dates of marketed drugs to address shortages.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams responsible for marketed drug products must review and apply the guidance to remain compliant with sections C.010.014 to C.10.021 of the Food and Drug Regulations.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Register of Innovative Drugs
entries.description: A listing of drugs pursuant to sub-section C.08.004.1(9) of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.summary: A new register lists drugs identified as innovative under sub-section C.08.004.1(9) of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams must monitor this register to ensure they are aware of any drugs classified as innovative and comply with any related obligations.

entries.label: EMA Guidelines
entries.title: European Medicines Agency pre-authorisation procedural advice for users of the centralised procedure
entries.description: European Medicines Agency pre-authorisation procedural advice for users of the centralised procedure
entries.summary: EMA provides procedural advice for users of the centralised procedure.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams should review and align their application processes with the new procedural guidance.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Drug Product Database data extract [2026-10-05]
entries.description: The Drug Product Database (DPD) extract files contain complete product information for all approved, marketed and cancelled products, for human, veterinary, disinfectant and radiopharmaceutical use.
entries.summary: The Drug Product Database now provides data extracts containing complete product information for all approved, marketed and cancelled products across human, veterinary, disinfectant and radiopharmaceutical categories.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams need to be aware that they can access comprehensive product data for all therapeutic areas, impacting their regulatory submissions and compliance checks.

entries.title: EMA Management Board: highlights of September 2026 meeting

entries.title: Global regulators call for advancing alternatives to animal testing across the medicine lifecycle

entries.why_it_matters: RA teams should anticipate future regulatory expectations to develop and document alternative testing strategies.

entries.title: Women are missing from medicines development: EMA’s roadmap for change

But the momentum to improve support for women’s health has never been stronger.…,         Meaningful change starts with dialogue and with a shared understanding of the challenges we face. We end this workshop with a clear path to action”, “National regulatory…,   The multistakeholder workshop, broadcast live, brought together over 100 leading voices on women’s health at EU and international level, from regulators to patients, healthcare…

entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must prepare for new guidance that will require incorporating gender-specific data and considerations into clinical trials and regulatory submissions.

entries.title: Updated Register of Certificates of Supplementary Protection and Applications
entries.description: Listing of drugs pursuant to sub-section 120(1) of the Certificate of Supplementary Protection Regulations.
entries.summary: The register of drugs eligible for supplementary protection certificates has been updated.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams should review the updated list to ensure correct SPC filing timelines for affected drugs.

entries.title: Member states contact points for review of national implementation of quick response (QR) codes of veterinary medicinal products authorised via the centralised (CP), mutual recognition (MRP), decentralised procedures (DCP) and national procedures
entries.description: Member states contact points for review of national implementation of quick response (QR) codes of veterinary medicinal products authorised via the centralised (CP), mutual recognition (MRP), decentralised procedures (DCP) and national procedures
entries.summary: Member states have designated contact points for reviewing how national QR code implementation is applied to veterinary medicinal products authorised through the centralised, mutual recognition, decentralised and national procedures.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams need to be aware of these contact points to coordinate compliance and resolve implementation issues with national authorities.

entries.title: Monthly update to the generic submissions under review list

entries.why_it_matters: RA teams should note changes to the list to track review status of their generic applications.

entries.label: EMA Guidelines
entries.title: Substances considered as not falling within the scope of Regulation (EC) No. 470/2009, with regard to residues of veterinary medicinal products in foodstuffs of animal origin

entries.why_it_matters: RA teams handling veterinary residue compliance must now identify which substances are not subject to the regulation and adjust monitoring and reporting accordingly.

entries.title: Pharmacovigilance-related regulatory recommendations for centrally authorised veterinary medicinal products during 2026

entries.summary: New pharmacovigilance recommendations will apply to all centrally authorised veterinary medicinal products from 2026.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams must update their pharmacovigilance processes for veterinary products to comply with the new centrally-authorised product guidance.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Compliance and enforcement policy for health products (POL-0001)
entries.description: This policy describes Health Canada's national compliance and enforcement approach for health products regulated under the Food and Drugs Act and its regulations.

entries.why_it_matters: All RA teams dealing with Health Products must align their compliance processes to the updated policy.
